newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark dips below 1.70 after a steady U.S. noon.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark dips below 1.70 after a steady U.S. noon.

text.p: The dollar stood nearly unchanged against the mark and slightly higher versus the yen at noon, but sizeable selling by funds shoved the dollar below 1.70 marks shortly after midday, dealers said.
"We're hearing some funds are selling it, there is no real sexy fundamental story here," said Keith Woodfin, currency analyst at Foreign Exchange Analytics.

At midday, the dollar was trading at 1.7032/37 marks, barely up from 1.7030/40 at the open, and at 125.62/72 yen, up from 125.18/28. But the dollar then slumped to 1.6960 marks, as the large order went through a thin market, traders said.
The greenback was heavy against the mark for most of the morning but firmed versus the yen.
The German currency extended overnight gains on the yen and lira and mark/French continued to make headway after France was put on election alert.
"I'd say flows in those crosses are tending to wash through dollar/mark and keep that a little unstable," said Dennis Pettit, foreign exchange manager at Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan.
"Mark/yen is also bid, so it's a reflection of mark strength," Pettit added.

The mark rose as high as 3.3772 French francs in the U.S. on Monday, amid preparations by French President Jacques Chirac to call an early parliamentary election. Dealers saw the election as an effort to allow the government to pass tough austerity measures for participation in European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

Meanwhile, mark/lira rose to the 997 area. The Italian currency continued to suffer from reports that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had criticized Italy's proposed mini-budget, which was designed to bolster Italy's chances of qualifying for the single currency.
With mark and French franc yields close to parity, dealers said there was no incentive to invest in francs with the uncertainty of a looming election.
"Mark and French interest rates are basically the same and people just don't see the reason to hold French francs over marks right now," said Bill Bertha, chief dealer at Mellon Bank.
"Couple that with the criticism of Italy's budget by the IMF and the lira's weak against the mark too," he continued.
Mark/yen also continued to edge higher during the morning, closing in on the 73.75 level after rising to 73.69 overnight.

Profit-taking from last week's run up to a cyclical high at 1.7375 marks may have also weighed on the dollar, as the market pared long-dollar positions ahead of the weekend Group of Seven meeting in Washington, experts said.

"Some squaring of positions ahead of G7 is something that is not all that unusual, particularly given the scope of the dollar's gains last week," said Bob Lynch, senior currency analyst at MMS International.
Dealers also said the G7 meeting was keeping dollar/yen trade uneventful, with steady bidding interest seen near 125.
Elsewhere, the dollar eased to 1.4470/80 Swiss francs from 1.4488/98 at the open and stood unchanged at Canadian $1.3973/78.
